10.0.s.en: (1) The death of Nadab and Abihu

10.0.0.en: Censer: a metal vessel in which burning coal is placed with grains of incense (a thurible) on top. The two sons of Aaron the priest, "Nadab and Abihu," were so bold as to break God's law by offering strange fire inside the sanctuary, and they did not take from the divine fire that had come out from the tabernacle of the congregation to the bronze altar (ch. 9:24). This strange fire signifies the fire of the passions or the teachings foreign to the Church, with which we cannot enter before God.

10.0.1.en: In addition, offering incense in the censer was the work of the high priest, while the priests offered incense and fire in other holy vessels (Ex 30). The elders of the Jews think that they were in a state of drunkenness, because this chapter stipulates that the priest is not to be drunk (vv. 8, 9). It is very regrettable that two of the great ones of the people, who were priests, should fall into a clear violation of God's commands a very short time after their ordination.

10.0.2.en: Be careful about what you teach others, which is the teachings of the Church that you received from her, and if you do not know something, do not presume to give rulings or advice whose correctness you do not know, but ask those who are more experienced than you, and that not only in spiritual and church matters but in any subject of life, so that you are wise and people respect your opinion and you cause no one to stumble.

10.1.0.en: We see here that the blessed fire of the Lord that accepted the sacrifices turns into a deadly fire to discipline the sinner, and this is a proof of God's justice and holiness and His anger at the errors of His servants. Aaron's shock was great, but he submitted in silence. And God declared through Moses that He requires holiness and precision in obeying His commandments from all people, especially those near to Him such as the priests, and if they break His commandments they are punished more severely because they know God more than others.

10.2.0.en: Because it is not permitted for Aaron and his two remaining sons to take part in the procedures of mourning or burial, as they are occupied with their service, others of their relatives carried out the task, for the law of God requires that the priest not leave his service in the sanctuary for any reason however important, to show the greatness of God and His service. The two who buried Nadab and Abihu were their cousins, so Moses said to them "carry your brethren," since a cousin is called a brother, as it was said of the cousins of Christ that they were His brethren, and as is said now in the land of Egypt.

10.2.1.en: Nadab and Abihu were carried in their priestly garments, which were probably not burned by the fire, as a showing by God of the dignity of the priesthood, although this is contrary to the nature of fire, which burns everything before it.

10.3.0.en: Moses commanded them to raise their feelings above the human level, as the Lord commanded Ezekiel the prophet at the death of his wife (Ezek 24:15-18), and not to practice the pagan customs in mourning for relatives, for the feelings of the priest belong first to God, and then to all people and are not limited to his relatives. The going out of the priests to bury Nadab and Abihu would prevent them from practicing their priestly service, since they would be made unclean by touching the dead as the Law prescribes, and there were no other priests. God also wished to show the heinousness of the sin of Nadab and Abihu in breaking God's law, so the people nearest to them, their father and their brothers, did not take part in burying them, but He allowed the whole people at the same time to take care of burying them and to weep for them in honor of their priesthood.

10.3.1.en: Despite the small number of consecrated priests, two of them died, for God is exacting in choosing His servants however great the need of the service.

10.4.0.en: Wine: grape juice that has fermented naturally.

10.4.1.en: Strong drink: grape juice fermented so strongly that it makes the one who drinks it drunk, and it was perhaps made by distilling wine.

10.4.2.en: God forbids His priests to drink wine of all kinds before they enter the service of the tabernacle of the congregation, as abstinence from material things and so that they may be fully alert, in sanctification and reverence of the house of God.

10.4.3.en: From here we conclude that what drove the two sons of Aaron to error was perhaps their drinking wine to the point of drunkenness.

10.4.4.en: The meaning of this is that, although the priests may drink a little wine, that is, naturally fermented grape juice, with a very small percentage of alcohol, in their ordinary life, this is not permitted before they enter the service, while intoxicating wine, that is, strongly fermented, is not permitted in any case.

10.5.0.en: By not drinking wine the priests keep their balance so that they can practice the function of discernment and teaching, so that they distinguish between the unclean and the clean and complete their service with concentration, and are also able to guide the people and teach them God's commandments and laws. Drunkenness signifies immersion in the things and pleasures of the world to the point of losing balance and spiritual discernment.

10.5.1.en: Use the material things of the world, for they are God's gift to you, but do not immerse yourself in them lest they distract you from God and all your thinking becomes about them and your view of everything becomes material, so that you no longer long for spiritual things, but your conduct changes and becomes carnal, far from God.

10.6.s.en: (3) The priests' eating of their portion

10.6.0.en: Moses began to encourage Aaron and his sons to eat their portion of the offerings made by fire of the Lord (as explained before in ch. 8), because it seems that the grief in their hearts was intense over what had happened, and likewise their fear of God, and he confirmed the law, which is the eating of the unleavened bread in the house of the Lord (a holy place), and it is eaten by the priests only (ch. 6:14-18), while the priests' portion of the peace offerings, which is the right shoulder and the breast, they eat with their wives and sons and daughters in a clean place outside the tabernacle of the congregation.

10.6.1.en: Sin brings grief, but I must not stop at it; rather I wipe it away with repentance and regain my joy in the Lord.

10.7.s.en: (4) The burning of the goat of the sin offering

10.7.0.en: The two remaining sons of Aaron erred in the ritual of the sin offering, for they did not eat their portion of it but burned it, so Moses was angry with them and rebuked them so that they would not neglect carrying out God's commands. This error is lighter than the error of their two brothers (v. 1), because the first was deliberate while this one was from forgetfulness. The priest's eating of the sin offering of the people was a proof of his sharing with his people in bearing their sin, and also that God had accepted the sacrifice and forgiven the sin (ch. 4:22, 27). And Moses reminded them that, as long as the blood of the goat of the sin offering was not brought into the sanctuary and the altar of incense anointed with it, the priest must eat his portion of it, from which it is understood that the priest's portion of the sin offering is not only permitted him to eat, but it is necessary that he eat it.

10.8.0.en: Such things have befallen me: the death of my two sons Nadab and Abihu.

10.8.1.en: Should it have been accepted in the sight of the Lord: Aaron asked whether God accepts that we eat of the sin offering while we are in grief over the death of Nadab and Abihu, or whether it would be considered an error, because we ought to eat of God's sacrifices with contentment and thanksgiving and joy, that is, he excuses himself for not eating of the goat lest he eat it in sorrow and sin against God. Aaron excused himself to Moses by saying that his two sons Eleazar and Ithamar had offered to the Lord the sacrifices that were required of them, but their state of mind, his and his sons', after what had befallen them of discipline from God by the death of their two brothers, did not allow them to share in eating of the sacrifice, because they felt they were bearing the sins of their two brothers who had died, so how could they bear with them the sins of the people and eat of the flesh of the goat? Therefore they left it to burn entirely on the bronze altar, and Moses accepted their excuse, because God bears the weakness of Eleazar and Ithamar but does not bear the pride of Nadab and Abihu.

10.8.2.en: Repentance washes away the sins of your shortcomings and neglect, so hasten to it that you may obtain forgiveness in the Sacrament of Confession and be strengthened to begin anew with care and vigor to make up for what you have missed, so that you grow in your love for God. Clean and unclean animals

11.0.0.en: Cheweth the cud: chews its food again after swallowing it to complete its digestion.

11.0.1.en: Hoof: the front of the animal's foot, which is either a single piece or cloven into two parts. The Book of Leviticus. God defined for Moses what is unclean and what is clean, as a Father concerned with every detail of our daily life. The definition included two conditions together, which are:

11.0.2.en: 1- Chewing the cud, and this points to careful meditation on the meanings of the word of God.

11.0.3.en: 2- The cloven hoof: which gives the animal the ability to walk for a longer time, so it signifies striving and perseverance in it. There is another opinion that the cloven hoof signifies discernment. The Book of Deuteronomy defined these clean animals (Deut 14).

11.0.4.en: I wish you would read the Holy Bible every day with care and understand its words and meditate on them to apply them in your life, and even repeat one verse throughout the day to live in it.

11.1.0.en: The coney: a small animal like the rabbit that lives in Palestine and dwells among the rocks, with sharp claws, and it signifies fierceness.

11.1.1.en: If the animal does not have the two preceding conditions, that is, if one of them is lacking, it is considered unclean. The camel and the coney and the hare do not have a cloven hoof, so they are not eaten, and the swine does not chew the cud, so it is considered unclean.

11.1.2.en: The hare and the coney are considered among the animals that chew the cud, since they move their jaws continually as though they were chewing the cud but without actual rumination, and this is because the commandment was given according to the way of life of the ordinary person and not according to specialized scientific study. The swine signifies uncleanness because of its wallowing in the mire and its eating of dirty foods.

11.2.0.en: The Law confirms not eating of the unclean animals even if one of the conditions is present in them, which is chewing the cud or the cloven hoof. And it forbids touching their carcasses after their death for two reasons:

11.2.1.en: 1- The connection of death with sin, since it is a result of it when God declared that in Paradise, so touching the dead makes unclean.

11.2.2.en: 2- A health benefit, because the carcass of an animal brings germs harmful to man.

11.3.1.en: It defines two conditions together for aquatic creatures:

11.3.2.en: 1- The presence of fins, as a reference to strength in movement and the ability to swim against the current. These are traits of the spiritual man.

11.3.3.en: 2- The presence of scales and shells that protect the body from the pressure of the water and the shocks of the rocks, as a reference to a person's resisting evil and fortifying himself with the various means of grace.

11.3.4.en: Those in which these two traits are present may be eaten, for they are clean, whereas those in which one of the two traits or both are lacking are considered unclean, so they are not eaten and touching their carcasses is not permitted.

11.3.5.en: Resist sin and keep away from its sources, and if you fall into it, rise quickly and do not despair, for your God loves you, and resistance is accomplished by prayer and reading and lowering yourself in humility before God with persistence until He rescues you from it, relying on the power of His Body and Blood.

11.4.0.en: The eagle: a large wild bird that snatches its prey, and it signifies theft.

11.4.1.en: The ossifrage: called the bearded vulture, it resembles the eagle, and it throws its victim from a height to shatter it, and it signifies cruelty. The osprey: a coastal bird that eats fish, and it signifies snatching.

11.4.2.en: The kite: a wild bird that lives by snatching and eating stinking carcasses, and it feeds on filth. The hawk: a wild bird of prey like the kite, with sharp sight. It signifies the use of gifts for evil. The raven: a wild bird that snatches prey and loves stinking carcasses, and it signifies theft and greed. The ostrich: a huge wild bird that does not sit on its eggs in the nest, and it signifies recklessness and not bearing responsibility.

11.4.3.en: The male ostrich: the male of the ostriches, which is more beautiful than the female. It signifies vain outward beauty. The gull: the seagull, a sea bird that snatches, which signifies theft and greed.

11.4.4.en: The falcon: like the hawk and used in hunting, and it signifies injustice.

11.4.5.en: The owl: a wild night bird, and it signifies ruin because of its living in ruins.

11.4.6.en: The cormorant: a coastal bird that dives to snatch fish, and it signifies theft.

11.4.7.en: The crane: a large long-legged bird that cries out much, and it signifies noise and restlessness. The pelican: a strong bird of prey that loves swimming, and it signifies fierceness.

11.4.8.en: Al-Qawq: a water bird like the swan, and it signifies ruin.

11.4.9.en: The vulture: a bird of prey like the eagle, and it signifies evil.

11.4.10.en: The stork: a bird that eats frogs and insects, long-beaked and long-legged. It signifies uncleanness and lack of care.

11.4.11.en: The parrot: a predatory bird that imitates speech, and it signifies lightness of mind.

11.4.12.en: The hoopoe: a skillful wild bird that eats worms and insects, and it signifies hypocrisy and outward beauty. The bat: one of the flying mammals, and it is a bird of prey, and among its kinds are blood-sucking ones, and it signifies parasitism.

11.4.13.en: It defines the traits of the unclean birds as being predatory, fierce in nature, and eating carrion, that is, stinking carcasses and filth, despite the beauty of their outward appearance. They point to the traits of the wicked and their hypocrisy as mentioned in the preceding description of the birds, and they show the necessity of the purity of the source of our teaching and our spiritual food, and the necessity of gentleness and of not harming others.

11.5.1.en: Creeping thing of the fowl: birds that walk on the ground with their feet.

11.5.2.en: Legs: the leg above the foot.

11.5.3.en: The locust, the bald locust, the beetle, the grasshopper: stages of the locust.

11.5.4.en: It adds a new attribute to the forbidden birds, which is the inability to fly and being content to walk on the ground, "creeping," as a reference to the lack of spiritual elevation and attachment to earthly things. As for insects, the flying are clean and the creeping unclean, for the same reason, which is that it signifies the lack of spiritual elevation.

11.6.0.en: The inspired text forbids eating the animals that do not have a cloven hoof or do not chew the cud, because they are unclean, and it also forbids touching their carcasses after their death lest a person become unclean.

11.7.0.en: It adds to the unclean animals those of the four-footed that go upon their paws, such as the dog and the cat and the mouse and the monkey, as a reference to the uncleanness of a person's being bound wholly to earthly things and attached to them. The Book of Leviticus. And whoever touches or carries the carcass of an unclean bird or animal becomes unclean until the evening, so that he feels the wrong of sin and keeps away from the evil traits of the forbidden animals, and then he washes himself and his clothes with water as a symbol of the water of Baptism and the Sacrament of Repentance and Confession.

11.7.1.en: As much as you think of heaven and care for prayer, you are able to give up your material attachments and evil desires, so that you gradually rise and advance with steady steps toward eternity.

11.8.0.en: The weasel: an animal like a large mouse that lives by snatching, and it signifies theft. The mouse: it signifies destruction.

11.8.1.en: The spiny-tailed lizard: a green desert animal with a strong tail like the crocodile, and it signifies violence.

11.8.2.en: The gecko-like lizard: like the gecko, and it signifies uncleanness and lack of care.

11.8.3.en: The monitor lizard: a crawling animal with a long snout and a long tail that eats eggs, and it is like the chameleon, and very hostile to snakes. It signifies theft.

11.8.4.en: The lizard: a kind of reptile like the chameleon or the crocodile, and it signifies preying.

11.8.5.en: The small lizard: a kind of reptile like the chameleon, and it signifies clinging to the earth.

11.8.6.en: The chameleon: a kind of reptile that changes color to the color of its surroundings, and it signifies hypocrisy.

11.8.7.en: God gives a statement of the small animals that walk on four feet and the unclean reptiles. We notice what they signify of the traits of the wicked as explained before, and their sharing the trait of clinging to earthly things, so whoever touches their carcasses becomes unclean until the evening.

11.9.0.en: Sack: haircloth (a garment) of camel's hair or goat's hair.

11.9.1.en: It confirms here that any articles used in the house, if the carcass of a creeping thing falls on them, become unclean, so they should be put into water until the evening to be cleansed, and so God commands keeping away from the carcasses of the unclean animals because they signify sin, since death entered the world through sin, and they also carry diseases or infection that call for cleaning and cleansing what their carcasses fall upon. And the power of water to cleanse is a symbol of the power of Baptism in the forgiveness of sins.

11.10.0.en: If the carcass of a creeping thing falls on an earthen vessel with any liquids in it, it becomes unclean, and since earthenware absorbs the liquids that became unclean, it must be got rid of by breaking it, and likewise whatever it contained, because it became unclean. Likewise the carcass of a creeping thing makes unclean any liquid or food it touches.

11.11.1.en: Range for pots: the stove that was used anciently for cooking and heating, which is a barrier of brick inside which fire is kindled, and on top of it the vessel to be heated is held.

11.11.2.en: Likewise the oven or the range on which it falls is broken down, because it has become unclean.

11.12.0.en: As for wells and springs, their water is renewed from the groundwater, so they become clean, because the water that became unclean is thrown on the ground and new water from the groundwater takes its place. And the part of the water that became unclean and fell on the ground is drained away with the earth it fell on and thrown far away because it has become unclean. Here the Law confirms the heinousness of sin and its uncleanness.

11.13.0.en: The water becomes unclean by the carcass of the animal, and then the seeds absorb this water and become unclean and must be got rid of, whereas dry ones, when the carcass of an animal touches them, remain clean, because the carcass touches their outer husk and they are considered clean, since the seed changes when it is planted and becomes a plant through food and water and sun.

11.14.0.en: Carcasses are unclean even if they are of clean animals, for they are a symbol of bearing sin.

11.14.1.en: We also see the action of water in cleansing as before, so whoever touches them or eats of them unwittingly, not knowing that it was dead, or carries its carcass, becomes unclean until the evening and must wash with water.

11.15.0.en: The uncleanness of the reptiles that cling to the earth in their going, like snakes, points to attachment to earthly things, and likewise everything that goes on four feet or more; all these animals are unclean and are not eaten, with the exception of the clean animals that go on four feet and were mentioned before, such as cattle and goats and sheep.

11.16.0.en: The purity of the children of God is required as a condition of their sonship to the holy God, who brought them out of the places of uncleanness and out of Egypt, the land of idols, to make them saints, so that they keep away from touching the carcasses of creeping things or anything unclean.

11.17.0.en: Thus this chapter distinguished between everything that is clean and what is unclean, and between everything that is eaten and what is not permitted to be eaten. As for the law of the New Testament, it considered all of God's creation clean according to the vision of the Apostle Peter (Acts 10:11-13), since our Baptism has cleansed us and raised us up with a new holy nature.

11.17.1.en: Let us examine ourselves daily and search our souls lest some of these unclean traits creep into us and corrupt our spiritual life, and so that we may uproot from our souls, one by one, every plant that our heavenly Father has not planted. The purification of the mother
